questions.topic: Beyond syllabus: incentre, circumcentre and orthocentre of a triangle
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the special centers of a triangle:
Statement I: The Incenter is the only one of the three centers (Incenter, Circumcenter, Orthocenter) that is guaranteed to be strictly in the interior of every possible triangle.
Statement II: If the Circumcenter of a triangle lies in the exterior of the triangle, then the Orthocenter must also lie in the exterior of the triangle.
Statement III: A point that is equidistant from the three vertices of a triangle is the center of the inscribed circle (Incircle).

options.b: Only Statement I and II are correct
options.c: Only Statement II and III are correct

questions.solution: (B) Only Statement I and II are correct. The incentre is always inside; a circumcentre outside means the triangle is obtuse, so the orthocentre is also outside; III is false because the point equidistant from the vertices is the circumcentre, not the incentre.

marking_points.point: (B) Only Statement I and II are correct

questions.question:
Sanjana draw the following figure on a board where a circle is inscribed in a quadrilateral. Then she wrote the following relationships.
I. ZW + WX = XY + YZ
II. ZY + WX = ZW + YX
Which of the above relationships is/are DEFINITELY true?
(Figure: circle with centre O inscribed in quadrilateral ZYXW — Z top-left, Y top-right, X bottom-right, W bottom-left — touching ZY at R, YX at Q, XW at P and WZ at S.)
questions.solution: (B) only II. Tangents from an external point are equal, so for a quadrilateral circumscribing a circle the sums of opposite sides are equal: ZY + WX = ZW + YX. Relation I adds adjacent sides and need not hold.

questions.topic: Angles in a semicircle, angle at centre, cyclic quadrilateral test
questions.question:
In the adjoining diagram ∠DOE = 46° and ∠BGH = 113°
i. Find ∠DBC and ∠DCE
ii. Prove that CBGH is a cyclic quadrilateral.
(Figure: AB is a diameter of the circle with centre O; D and E lie on the upper semicircle; AD and BE produced meet at C outside the circle; G lies on the lower arc; H lies on CA produced, and HG and GB are joined; ∠DOE = 46°, ∠BGH = 113°.)
questions.solution:
i. ∠DBE = ½∠DOE = ½ × 46° = 23° (angle at centre is double the angle at the circumference), so ∠DBC = 23°. ∠ADB = 90° (angle in a semicircle), so ∠BDC = 90°. In △BDC, ∠DCB = 180° − 90° − 23° = 67°, i.e. ∠DCE = 67°. (Equivalently ∠ADB, the exterior angle, = ∠DCB + ∠DBC ⇒ 90° = ∠DCB + 23°.)
ii. ∠HCB = ∠DCB = 67° and ∠HGB = 113°. ∠HCB + ∠HGB = 67° + 113° = 180°. Since a pair of opposite angles of quadrilateral CBGH is supplementary, CBGH is cyclic.
questions.figure_desc: Circle with diameter AB and centre O; D, E on the upper arc with ∠DOE = 46°; AD and BE produced meet at C; G on the lower arc with ∠BGH = 113°, H on CA produced.

questions.question: Prove that (sin A − cos A + 1)/(sin A + cos A − 1) = cos A/(1 − sin A)
questions.solution:
LHS = (sin A − cos A + 1)/(sin A + cos A − 1) × (1 − sin A)/(1 − sin A).
Numerator = (sin A − cos A + 1)(1 − sin A) = sin A − cos A + 1 − sin²A + sin A cos A − sin A = (1 − sin²A) − cos A + sin A cos A = cos²A − cos A + sin A cos A = cos A (cos A − 1 + sin A).
So LHS = cos A (sin A + cos A − 1) / [(sin A + cos A − 1)(1 − sin A)] = cos A/(1 − sin A) = RHS. Hence proved.

marking_points.point: multiply numerator and denominator by (1 − sin A)
factor numerator as cos A(sin A + cos A − 1)
cancel to get cos A/(1 − sin A)

questions.question: Use properties of proportion for the following: If (x³ + 12x)/(6x² + 8) = (y³ + 27y)/(9y² + 27), find x : y.
questions.solution:
By componendo and dividendo: (x³ + 6x² + 12x + 8)/(x³ − 6x² + 12x − 8) = (y³ + 9y² + 27y + 27)/(y³ − 9y² + 27y − 27) ⇒ (x + 2)³/(x − 2)³ = (y + 3)³/(y − 3)³ ⇒ (x + 2)/(x − 2) = (y + 3)/(y − 3).
Applying componendo and dividendo again: 2x/4 = 2y/6 ⇒ x/2 = y/3 ⇒ x/y = 2/3. Hence x : y = 2 : 3.

marking_points.point: take cube roots and apply C–D again: 2x/4 = 2y/6

questions.topic: Investment, sale and reinvestment in shares
questions.question:
Mrs. Kulkarni invested ₹19,200 in 15 % ₹100 shares at 20 % discount. After a year she sold these shares at ₹90 each and invested the proceeds (including her dividend) in 20 % ₹50 shares at ₹42. Find:
i. the dividend for the 1st year
ii. her annual income in the second year
iii. sale proceeds
iv. the percentage change in her return of her original investment.
questions.solution:
M.V. = ₹100 − 20% of ₹100 = ₹80. Number of shares = 19200/80 = 240.
i. Dividend (1st year) = 240 × 15% × 100 = ₹3,600.
iii. Sale proceeds = 240 × ₹90 = ₹21,600; including the dividend, the amount reinvested = 21600 + 3600 = ₹25,200 (the answer key reports ₹25,200 as the sale proceeds including dividend).
ii. New shares = 25200/42 = 600. Annual income (2nd year) = 600 × 20% × 50 = ₹6,000.
iv. Change in income = 6000 − 3600 = ₹2,400. Percentage change in return on original investment = 2400/19200 × 100 = 12.5% (return rises from 18.75% to 31.25%, an increase of 12.5 percentage points).

questions.question:
A game stall at a funfair uses a special die whose six faces are marked 2, 4, 4, 7, 9, 12.
A player rolls the die once. The stall owner announces the following rules:
• If the score is 7 or more, the player wins a silver token.
• If the score is 4, the player gets another chance to roll.
• Any other score means no reward.
i. How many different scores are possible when the die is rolled?
ii. What is the probability that the player gets another chance to roll?
iii. What is the probability that the player wins a silver token?
questions.solution:
n(S) = 6 equally likely faces: {2, 4, 4, 7, 9, 12}.
i. Different scores possible = {2, 4, 7, 9, 12} = 5. (The answer key writes this as P = 5/6, but the question asks for a count: 5.)
ii. Score 4 appears on 2 faces: P = 2/6 = 1/3.
iii. Score ≥ 7: {7, 9, 12} = 3 faces: P = 3/6 = 1/2.

questions.topic: Nature of roots — range of k for non-real roots
questions.question:
The quadratic equation below is being analyzed by Pratham, Juhi, and Veer:
(2k − 1)x² − 4kx + (2k + 3) = 0.
They are asked to determine a value of the constant k that ensures the equation has non-real roots.
i. Pratham claims the value is k = −1.
ii. Juhi claims the value is k = 0.75.
iii. Veer claims the value is k = 1.
Which student's claim is correct? Justify your answer with proper working.
questions.solution:
a = 2k − 1, b = −4k, c = 2k + 3. For non-real roots, D = b² − 4ac < 0.
D = 16k² − 4(2k − 1)(2k + 3) = 16k² − 4(4k² + 4k − 3) = −16k + 12.
−16k + 12 < 0 ⇒ k > 3/4 = 0.75.
k = −1: D = 28 > 0 (real, distinct roots) — Pratham wrong. k = 0.75: D = 0 (real, equal roots) — Juhi wrong. k = 1: D = −4 < 0 (non-real roots; also a = 1 ≠ 0) — Veer is correct.

marking_points.point: identify a, b, c and condition D < 0
conclude Veer (k = 1) is correct; others rejected

questions.question: Solve for x using properties of proportion: 16[(a − x)/(a + x)]³ = (a + x)/(a − x).
questions.solution:
16(a − x)³/(a + x)³ = (a + x)/(a − x) ⇒ (a − x)⁴/(a + x)⁴ = 1/16 ⇒ (invertendo) (a + x)⁴/(a − x)⁴ = 16 ⇒ (a + x)/(a − x) = ±2.
Case +2: componendo–dividendo ⇒ 2a/2x = 3/1 ⇒ x = a/3.
Case −2: componendo–dividendo ⇒ 2a/2x = (−2 + 1)/(−2 − 1) = 1/3 ⇒ x = 3a.
Hence x = a/3 or x = 3a.

questions.question:
Aashi, Viyaan, and Tisha are discussing the slope (or gradient) of the line segment connecting two points, A and B, on a coordinate plane. They are given the coordinates of the two points as A(4, −1) and B(x, 7).
1. Aashi claims the slope of the line is 2.
2. Viyaan claims the line is perpendicular to the line y = −3x + 5.
3. Tisha claims that for the line to be vertical, the value of x must be 4.
Answer the following questions based on the scenario:
i. If Aashi's claim is correct, what must be the value of x?
ii. If Viyaan's claim is correct, what must be the value of x?
iii. Is Tisha's claim correct? Explain your reasoning.
questions.solution:
Slope of AB = (7 − (−1))/(x − 4) = 8/(x − 4).
i. 8/(x − 4) = 2 ⇒ x − 4 = 4 ⇒ x = 8.
ii. Slope of y = −3x + 5 is −3; perpendicular slope = 1/3. 8/(x − 4) = 1/3 ⇒ x − 4 = 24 ⇒ x = 28.
iii. Yes. A vertical line (parallel to the y-axis) has all points with the same x-coordinate; A has x = 4, so B must have x = 4 (slope 8/0 is undefined).

i. Prove that △PAB ∼ △PCD
ii. Find the length of CD.
(Figure: chords AD and BC of a circle intersect at P inside the circle; AB and CD are joined.)

ii. Corresponding sides are proportional: PA/PC = AB/CD ⇒ 7.5/5 = 9/CD ⇒ CD = 9 × 5/7.5 = 6 cm.

questions.question: A well of inner diameter 8 m, is dug up 14 m deep. The earth taken out of it is spread evenly all round it to width of 3 m to form an embankment. Find the height of this embankment.
questions.solution:
Well: r = 4 m, H = 14 m. Embankment: outer radius R = 4 + 3 = 7 m, inner radius r = 4 m.

questions.topic: Combined inequation on a number line
questions.question:
Solve the inequation and represent the solution set on a number line.
2x − 3 ≥ (1 − x)/3 + x ≥ 4x/3 − 5, x ∈ R.
questions.solution:
First part: 2x − 3 ≥ (1 − x)/3 + x ⇒ 6x − 9 ≥ 1 + 2x ⇒ 4x ≥ 10 ⇒ x ≥ 5/2.
Second part: (1 − x)/3 + x ≥ 4x/3 − 5 ⇒ 1 + 2x ≥ 4x − 15 ⇒ 16 ≥ 2x ⇒ x ≤ 8.
Solution set = {x : 2½ ≤ x ≤ 8, x ∈ R}. On the real number line: a solid (filled) dot at 2.5 and at 8 joined by a thick line.

marking_points.point: solution set 2.5 ≤ x ≤ 8 drawn with closed dots on the number line

questions.topic: Similar triangles with parallel lines; ratio of areas
concepts: ratio of areas = square of ratio of sides
questions.question:
In △ABC and △EDC, AB ∥ ED. BD = (1/3)BC, and AB = 12.3 cm
i. Prove that △ABC ∼ △EDC
ii. Find DE
iii. Find (area of △EDC)/(area of △ABC)
(Figure: triangle ABC with D on BC and E on AC, DE parallel to AB.)
questions.solution:
i. In △ABC and △EDC: ∠ABC = ∠EDC (corresponding angles, AB ∥ ED); ∠ACB = ∠ECD (common). So △ABC ∼ △EDC (AA).
ii. Let BD = x, BC = 3x, so DC = 2x. AB/ED = BC/DC ⇒ 12.3/DE = 3x/2x ⇒ DE = 12.3 × 2/3 = 8.2 cm.
iii. area △EDC / area △ABC = (DC/BC)² = (2/3)² = 4/9.

questions.question:
In an auditorium, seats were arranged in row and columns. The number of rows was equal to the number of seats in each row. When the number of rows was doubled and the number of seats in each row was reduced by 10, the total number of seats increased by 300. Find
i. the number of rows in the original arrangement.
ii. the number of seats in the auditorium after rearrangement.
questions.solution:
Let rows = seats per row = x; total = x².
New: 2x rows, (x − 10) seats per row ⇒ 2x(x − 10) = x² + 300 ⇒ x² − 20x − 300 = 0 ⇒ (x − 30)(x + 10) = 0 ⇒ x = 30 (x = −10 rejected).
i. Original rows = 30.
ii. Seats after rearrangement = 60 × 20 = 1,200.

questions.question:
The figure below (not drawn to scale) represents the line y = x + 1 and √3x − y = 1. Write down the angles that the line makes with positive direction of the x - axis. Hence determine angle θ.
(Figure: the two lines intersect in the first quadrant; θ is the acute angle between them at the point of intersection.)
questions.solution:
y = x + 1: slope 1 = tan 45°, so inclination 45°.
√3x − y = 1 ⇒ y = √3x − 1: slope √3 = tan 60°, so inclination 60°.
In the triangle formed with the x-axis, the exterior angle 60° = θ + 45° ⇒ θ = 15°.

questions.topic: Angle bisectors meeting the circumcircle (angles in same segment)
questions.question:
A triangle ABC is inscribed in a circle. The bisectors of ∠BAC, ∠ABC, and ∠ACB meet the circumcircle of △ABC at points P, Q and R respectively. Prove that
i. ∠ABC = 2∠APQ
ii. ∠ACB = 2∠APR
iii. ∠QPR = 90° − ½∠BAC
questions.solution:
Let ∠ABC = 2x, ∠ACB = 2z, ∠BAC = 2y; BQ, CR, AP are the bisectors.
i. ∠APQ = ∠ABQ (angles in the same segment AQ) = x, so ∠ABC = 2x = 2∠APQ.
ii. ∠APR = ∠ACR (angles in the same segment AR) = z, so ∠ACB = 2z = 2∠APR.
iii. ∠QPR = ∠APQ + ∠APR = x + z. In △ABC, 2x + 2z + ∠BAC = 180° ⇒ x + z = 90° − ½∠BAC. Hence ∠QPR = 90° − ½∠BAC.

marking_points.point: ∠QPR = x + z = 90° − ½∠BAC using angle sum

questions.topic: Lead shots dropped into a conical vessel
questions.question: A vessel is in the form of an inverted cone. Its height is 11 cm and the radius of its top which is open is 2.5 cm. It is filled with water upto rim. When lead shots, each of which is a sphere of radius 0.25 cm, are dropped into the vessel, 2/5 of the water flows out. Find the number of lead shots dropped in the vessel.
questions.solution:
Volume of cone = ⅓π(2.5)²(11). Water overflowing = ⅖ × ⅓π(2.5)²(11).
Volume of one shot = ⁴⁄₃π(0.25)³.
n × ⁴⁄₃π(0.25)³ = ⅖ × ⅓π(2.5)² × 11 ⇒ n = (2/5 × 6.25 × 11)/(4 × 0.015625) = 27.5/0.0625 = 440.
Number of lead shots = 440.

marking_points.point: n × volume of one sphere = overflow

questions.topic: Angle of elevation from eye level
questions.question:
With reference to the figure, a man stands on the ground at a point A, which is at the same horizontal plane as B, the foot of a vertical pole BC. The height of the pole is 10 m. The man's eye is 2 m above the ground. He observes the angle of elevation at C, the top of the pole as x°, where tan x° = 2/5. Find
i. the distance AB
ii. the angle of elevation of the top of the pole when he is standing 15 m from the pole. Give your answer to the nearest degree.
(Figure: AD = 2 m is the man (eye at D), DE horizontal meeting pole BC at E, ABED a rectangle.)
questions.solution:
ABED is a rectangle, so BE = AD = 2 m and AB = DE. CE = 10 − 2 = 8 m.
i. In △DEC, tan x° = CE/DE ⇒ 2/5 = 8/DE ⇒ DE = 20 m. So AB = 20 m.
ii. Now DE = 15 m: tan θ = 8/15 = 0.5333 ⇒ θ ≈ 28°4′ ≈ 28° (nearest degree).

questions.topic: Ogive — median, lower quartile, count above a value
questions.question:
Use graph paper for this question. A survey regarding height (in cm) of 60 boys belonging to class 10 of a school was conducted. The following data was recorded.
Height (in cm): 135-140, 140-145, 145-150, 150-155, 155-160, 160-165, 165-170
No. of boys: 4, 8, 20, 14, 7, 6, 1
Taking 2 cm = height of 10 cm along one axis and 2 cm = 10 boys along the other axis draw an ogive of the above distribution. Use the graph to estimate the following
i. the median
ii. lower quartile
iii. If above 158 cm is considered as the tall boys of the class. Find the number of boys in the class who are tall.
questions.solution:
Cumulative frequencies (less than upper boundary): 140→4, 145→12, 150→32, 155→46, 160→53, 165→59, 170→60. Plot (135, 0), (140, 4), (145, 12), (150, 32), (155, 46), (160, 53), (165, 59), (170, 60) with the given scale (a kink on the x-axis since it starts at 135) and join with a smooth free-hand curve.
i. N = 60; median = (N/2)th = 30th boy. From the graph median ≈ 150 cm (linear interpolation gives 149.5 cm).
ii. Lower quartile = (N/4)th = 15th boy ≈ 146 cm (interpolation 145.75 cm).
iii. At 158 cm the ogive reads ≈ 50 boys, so tall boys ≈ 60 − 50 = 10.
